seo.metaDescription: Plan against actual for each row: a hatched bar for the plan, a solid bar for the actual, and a delta that is colored by whether the change is good news.

props.markdown: Plan against actual, one row per item. The plan is a hatched bar, the actual is a solid bar, and the difference is written next to them and colored by whether it is good news.

Use `ComparisonBars` for budgets, estimates, quotas or targets, where each row has an expected value and a real one: job costs, hours, revenue by region. Set `good` to say which direction is good news. `good="down"` (the default) suits costs and hours, where under plan is good. `good="up"` suits revenue, where over plan is good. Rows within `tolerance` of the plan read “On plan” (change the text with `onPlanLabel`), and the part of an overrun beyond the plan is drawn apart from the solid bar. For a plain ranking without a plan, use `RankedBars`.
Costs with `good="down"`: Labor and Permits are over plan, so their deltas are the bad news, and Materials, under plan, is the good news.
Revenue with `good="up"`: over plan is the good news here. `onSelect` makes the rows selectable, so this example is a client component.

The chart is a single tab stop. Tabbing in shows the first row with its tooltip and announces it. Arrow keys move between rows, `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active row when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active row. `Esc` is only consumed when a row is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each row the keyboard moves to, in the form “1 of 6, Labor, plan $640, actual $1,060, +$420”: the position, the label, both values and the difference. The values and the delta are also in a visually hidden data table after the chart.

`ComparisonBars` picks its layout from the measured width: columns when the bars get at least 120 px between the label and the values, stacked rows otherwise. On a server-rendered page a narrow screen first renders columns at the 640 px default and switches to stacked after hydration. To avoid the jump, pass `initialWidth` or an explicit `layout`.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
